prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms, which made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: B033 alone, credited to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. The first-round exchange did not weaken the science. The chain from incretin physiology and proglucagon processing, through the identity and actions of the active truncated GLP-1 peptide and its receptor, to drugs with large randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity and cardiovascular and renal disease, is original, mature and independently confirmed. The chair asked whether the achievement is the physiology or the drug development. I answer that the prize-defining discovery is the physiology, and that the citation can say the therapies followed from it without crediting the molecules. That keeps the citation honest about what is being rewarded and keeps the allocation to three names defensible.
statement.case_against: The credit questions remain real and I have not resolved them. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide against Habener and colleagues cannot be settled from the shortlist and the round-1 statements, and several of us, myself included, are leaning on recalled priority histories. Excluding Knudsen is a deliberate choice, not a neutral one, and a reader who sees semaglutide as the achievement will call a physiology-only trio incomplete. I would say so openly in the committee record. A single-part prize also uses all three slots on one field, so it forgoes any second achievement, and that is a cost I accept.

responses.point: Thomas argues that replacing Mojsov with Knudsen would turn the prize into a drug-development award, and he holds that the clarity of the physiological discovery and the three-person cap favour Holst, Drucker and Mojsov.
responses.response: I agree, and I sharpen my own round-1 position. I had left Knudsen as the point to revisit if Mojsov's priority could not be defended. On reflection, Knudsen would not repair a Mojsov problem but would change the citation to a different achievement, as Thomas and Wahren-Herlenius both say. If Mojsov's claim proved untenable, the more coherent response would be to reconsider the configuration openly, not to move Knudsen in quietly. I therefore treat Knudsen as a recorded, deliberate exclusion and no longer as a default fallback for the third slot.

responses.point: Marie holds that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is distinct enough to credit, with some uncertainty, and that the committee should examine Habener's claim directly instead of assuming it away.
responses.response: I share that judgement and the uncertainty. My reasoning is that identifying and making the truncated active form was a necessary step between Holst's incretin physiology and Drucker's work on receptor biology and peptide actions, so it is a part of the physiology chain and not an ornament to it. The record in front of us cannot show whether Habener's contribution was equal, and I will not claim it does. My position is to credit Mojsov and say the priority question is unresolved in the record, which is more candid than dropping her because the case is contested. If a member can show from the record that Habener's claim is equal and decisive, I would want the committee to discuss it before the vote.

responses.point: Rickard keeps B048 (UPR) as an alternative, saying it is the stronger fundamental discovery than the HPV vaccine, and also agrees that Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a separate line from the core CAR invention.
responses.response: I agree on CAR-T, and I would credit only June and Sadelain on that part if it were ever needed. Where I still differ is on B048. Walter and Mori are a coherent pair and the mechanism is as clean as any on the list. But the link from the UPR to a changed medical practice is indirect, and I take your own point that its field impact lies mainly in basic cell biology. I keep it as a credible future candidate. It is not a competitor to B033 this year, and for that reason I leave it off my alternatives and name B026 and B007.

responses.point: The chair asked whether a two-part prize is acceptable if the three-person cap would cut the GLP-1 part to fewer than three names, and which second candidate would be proposed.
responses.response: I considered it seriously and I decline. A two-part prize with B026 would cut GLP-1 to two names, and the only coherent cut would drop either Mojsov, whose credit is already contested, or one of the other two physiology contributors. That damages the strongest configuration to add a second part that carries its own gap, since Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept falls outside June and Sadelain. I would only revisit this if the committee decided that CAR-T is at least as secure as B033, and nothing in round 1 supports that. B026 stays my lead alternative, and B007 my second, because the discovery and impact are large even though six names cannot fit into three places.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide against Habener can be defended; the record supplied does not settle it and I rely partly on memory.
Whether other members will hold that the achievement is the drug development, in which case Knudsen's exclusion becomes the central dispute and the citation would need to change.
If GLP-1 does not secure a majority, whether B026 with June and Sadelain is acceptable with a citation that is candid about Eshhar and the separate Rosenberg line.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My documented connections are a 2019 Physiological Reviews synthesis with Sten Grillner, collaboration with Patrik Ernfors, and a 2009 paper with Thomas Perlmann on stem-cell-derived dopamine neurons. None involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and Perlmann is a fellow committee member, not a candidate. I disclose no new conflict and see no need for recusal.
